Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level context**: [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1)\n- **Technical architecture**: [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1)\n-- **Workflows (authoritative behavioural spec)**: [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1) and the other files inside `odoo/_workflows`.\n- **Module READMEs**: each module may have a `README.md` under `odoo/<module>/README.md` with implementation notes and expectations.\n-- **Install logs / historical notes**: `_logs/` contains installation and setup notes per module.\n\n**Development Guidelines (how to implement changes)**\n- **Add/modify a model**: create/modify `models/*.py`, export package in `models/__init__.py`, add access rules in `security/ir.model.access.csv`, add any initial `data/*.xml` and register them in `__manifest__.py` `data` or `demo` lists, add views in `views/*.xml`, update `menu_items.xml` as needed, and add tests under `tests/`.\n- **Add a wizard or service**: put transient models under `wizards/` and views under `views/` (manifest `data`), keep service logic in modules like `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` when present (some modules include unit/functional tests).\n- **Run module tests**: use the Odoo test runner for module-level tests (e.g. `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable`) or your established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state  {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

 {"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/tournaments/<id>/feed`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/tournament/<id>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; remove fields\n  only in a new API version.\n- `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`: keep CSV column order and header\n  semantics stable for `finance_event_v1` until a new contract code/version is\n  published.\n- `/integration/v1/inbound/{contract_code}/deliveries`: keep\n  `delivery_outcome` semantics (`created`, `checksum_reuse`,\n  `idempotency_replay`) stable within v1.\n- JSON error envelopes for all managed integration endpoints must preserve the\n  typed shape `{error, error_code, correlation_id}` across minor releases.\n\nPartner onboarding references:\n\n- Golden request/response examples: `openapi/examples/INTEGRATION_GOLDEN_EXAMPLES.md`.\n- CI contract guardrails: `ci/check_openapi_contracts.py`.\n\n## Deprecation Policy\n\nThe working list of compatibility aliases, owners, review dates, and target\nsunset dates is maintained here and must be updated in the same change set as\nany contract-facing deprecation decision.\n\n| Surface | Canonical replacement | Target exit |\n|---|---|---|\n| `/tournaments`, `/tournaments/<slug>`, numeric tournament page routes | `/competitions`, `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric public tournament page routes | Edition routes under `/competitions/<edition-slug>` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Numeric or competition-named v1 tournament feeds | `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed` | 2026-10-01 |\n| Player import `name` column fallback | Explicit `first_name`, `last_name` columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Team import name fallbacks | `club_code` and explicit team naming columns | 2026-10-15 |\n| Participant import tournament/team name fallbacks | `tournament_code` and `team_code` | 2026-10-15 |\n\nRemove a compatibility surface only after its replacement is documented,\ncovered by tests, and announced in the owning module README. --db odoo --modules sports_federation_reporting,sports_federation_portal --dry-run\n```\n\n### Competition ownership change evidence\n\nThe legacy monolithic competition engine is removed from the The\nreplacement ownership chain is `sports_federation_competition_core`,\n`sports_federation_registration`, `sports_federation_format`,\n`sports_federation_calendar`, `sports_federation_scheduling`,\n`sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and `sports_federation_matchday`.\n\nBefore upgrading a database that previously installed the legacy engine:\n\n1. Take the database and filestore backups described above.\n2. Do not reinstall the removed engine as an ad-hoc rollback; use the\nreviewed database migration or rollback procedure for the target release.\n\n### Legacy ownership-removal review record\n\nThe repository-side review for this ownership change was completed against the\nrecorded base commit before preparing the release patch. The database restore drill remains mandatory before production upgrade;\nits output must be attached to the release ticket rather than inferred from\nrepository checks. No historical migration directory is reused for this\nownership removal, and no production record is silently rewritten.\n\nRollback is backup-based: stop the target release, preserve logs and the failed\ndatabase state for review, restore the pre-upgrade database and filestore, and\nrestart the previous release. If a data transformation is later required, it\nmust be introduced in a new reviewed migration with an explicit backfill and\nrollback plan; reinstalling the removed addon is not an approved rollback.\n\n## Backups\n\nThe upgrade script performs backups by default. It stores:\n\n- `modules.txt` with the exact install/upgrade module list\n- `<db>_<timestamp>.dump` as a PostgreSQL custom-format dump\n- `filestore_<db>_<timestamp>.tar.gz` when a filestore exists under\n  `./odoo-data/filestore/<db>`\n\nDo not use `--skip-backup` for production releases.\n\nRun the periodic restore drill against one of these backup directories before\nor during each release train using the restore checklist in this runbook:\n\n```bash\nbash addons/ci/restore_backup_drill.sh --backup-dir 2026-04-15_191410 --target-db odoo_restore_drill --dry-run\n```\n\n## Production Upgrade\n\nRun the upgrade and let the script restart the live Odoo service afterward so\nPython changes are loaded by the running web container:\n\n```bash\n./scripts/upgrade_sports_federation.sh --db odoo\n```\n\nFor a non-interactive upgrade that excludes demo data, use `--yes`. To include\nthe demo addon non-interactively, add `--install-demo`.\n\nThe script installs modules that are missing or uninstalled, upgrades modules\nthat are already installed, and restarts the Odoo service. It runs:\n\n- `odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <db> -i <install_module_csv> -u <upgrade_module_csv> --stop-after-init`\n- `docker compose restart odoo`\n\nThe demo addon is excluded by default. Interactive runs ask whether\n`sports_federation_demo` should be installed.  {"content": "# State And Ownership Matrix\n\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-05-20\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document records the canonical lifecycle states and ownership boundaries\nfor the federation records called out in the roadmap. It is intended to keep\ncontrollers, record rules, tests, and workflow docs aligned with the code.\n\n## Canonical records\n\n| Record | Module | Primary owner | Create path | Canonical states | Ownership boundary | Notes |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `federation.tournament` | `sports_federation_tournament` + `sports_federation_portal` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, scheduling services, website publication helpers | `draft`, `open`, `in_progress`, `closed`, `cancelled` | Federation-owned season / competition scope | Portal tournament workspaces only expose active tournaments (`open`, `in_progress`) and only for teams inside the user's current whole-club or explicit team scope. |\n| `federation.match` | `sports_federation_tournament` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, scheduling services, wizards | `draft`, `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled` | Federation-owned tournament/stage/group | Official standings inclusion is further gated by `include_in_official_standings` when `sports_federation_result_control` is installed. |\n| `federation.schedule.slot` | `sports_federation_calendar` | Calendar operations prepare capacity; scheduling assigns fixtures; approval publishes the resulting schedule | Match-day calendar and scheduling views | `available`, `break`, `blocked` | Federation-owned match day / playing-area scope | A slot belongs to one match day. Fixture assignment and overlap validation are enforced server-side. |\n| `federation.standing` | `sports_federation_standings` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, recompute/freeze actions | `draft`, `computed`, `frozen` | Federation-owned tournament/stage/group | Only computed or frozen standings are publication candidates. |\n| `federation.tournament.participant` | `sports_federation_tournament` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI or confirmed tournament registration | `registered`, `confirmed`, `withdrawn` | Team's club within a federation tournament | Portal users do not write participants directly; confirmed registrations may create them. |\n| `federation.competition.entry` | `sports_federation_portal` | Shared: club representative submits, federation staff reviews | Portal form or backend UI | `draft`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `rejected`, `cancelled` | Team must belong to one of the submitting user's represented clubs | This is the review buffer before participant creation. |\n| `federation.season.registration` | `sports_federation_base` + `sports_federation_portal` | Shared: club representative submits, federation staff confirms | Portal form or backend UI | `draft`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `cancelled` | Team must belong to one of the submitting user's represented clubs | Portal extension adds `submitted`, `user_id`, and `rejection_reason`. Rejecting a registration returns it to `draft`; there is no persistent `rejected` enum. |\n| `federation.finance.event` | `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Federation finance operations and approved workflow hooks | Backend UI or workflow automation | `draft`, `confirmed`, `settled`, `cancelled` | Source record remains authoritative; finance staff own settlement/cancellation | Season-registration confirmation and match finance hooks create events automatically. |\n\n## Archive behavior\n\nThe core master-data records now expose explicit archive and restore actions in\nthe backend UI so operational records do not disappear through ad hoc writes to\n`active`.\n\n| Record | Archive guardrail |\n| --- | --- |\n| `federation.club` | Clubs can only be archived after their active teams are archived. |\n| `federation.team` | Teams can only be archived when all linked season registrations are cancelled. |\n| `federation.season` | Open seasons must be closed or cancelled before they can be archived. |\n| `federation.tournament` | Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before they can be archived. |\n\n## Transition ownership\n\n| Record | Transition owners | Guardrails |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `federation.tournament` | Federation staff for lifecycle transitions; portal layer for read-only workspace access | Portal workspace helpers must revalidate both active-tournament scope and the caller's visible team or club scope before any elevated detail read. |\n| `federation.match` | Federation staff, scheduling services, result-control roles | Public routes are read-only. Match completion may trigger bracket advancement, and result-control transitions may trigger non-frozen standings recomputation. |\n| `federation.schedule.slot` | Calendar owns slot capacity and lifecycle; scheduling assigns fixtures; schedule approval publishes the resulting schedule | Slot availability and capacity are prepared by `sports_federation_calendar`; assignment validation is enforced by `sports_federation_scheduling`; approved schedules are immutable and published by `sports_federation_schedule_approval`. |\n| `federation.standing` | Federation staff | Frozen standings block recomputation unless forced. |\n| `federation.tournament.participant` | Federation staff, confirmed registration flow | Tournament/team eligibility is validated on create and update. |\n| `federation.competition.entry` | Portal club representatives for submission/cancel, federation staff for confirm/reject | Controllers validate club ownership and the model enforces ownership as defense in depth. |\n| `federation.season.registration` | Portal club representatives for submission/cancel, federation staff for confirm | Controllers validate club ownership and the model must enforce ownership as defense in depth. |\n| `federation.finance.event` | Federation finance staff for confirm/settle/cancel; Create a season and competition edition.\n2. Open registration and finalize the participant set.\n3. Freeze the competition structure and generate fixtures.\n4. Prepare match-day capacity and assign every fixture to a slot.\n5. Submit the schedule for independent review and publish the approved revision.\n6.  {"content": "# Sports Federation Discipline\n\nIncident reporting, disciplinary case management, sanctions, and player\nsuspensions. Provides the full disciplinary pipeline from incident detection\nthrough case resolution to sanction enforcement.\n\n## Purpose\n\nTracks **incidents** that occur during matches, groups them into **disciplinary\ncases** for investigation, and records **sanctions** (fines, warnings) and\n**suspensions** (match bans) as outcomes. Links back to players, clubs, and\nreferees for comprehensive disciplinary records.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Matches |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.match.incident`\n\nAn event that occurred during a match that may trigger disciplinary action.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Incident title |\n| `match_id` | Many2one | The match |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Involved player |\n| `club_id` | Many2one | Involved club |\n| `referee_id` | Many2one | Reporting referee |\n| `incident_type` | Selection | warning / yellow_card / red_card / misconduct / violence / admin_issue / other |\n| `minute_text` | Char | Match minute (text for flexibility) |\n| `description` | Text | What happened |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Linked disciplinary case |\n| `date_reported` | Date | When reported |\n| `reported_by_user_id` | Many2one | System user who filed it |\n| `status` | Selection | new / attached / closed |\n\n### `federation.disciplinary.case`\n\nAn investigation triggered by one or more incidents.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Case title |\n| `reference` | Char | Auto-sequence reference number |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / under_review / decided / appealed / closed |\n| `opened_on` / `decided_on` / `closed_on` | Date | Timeline |\n| `responsible_user_id` | Many2one | Case handler |\n| `incident_ids` | One2many | Related incidents |\n| `sanction_ids` | One2many | Resulting sanctions |\n| `suspension_ids` | One2many | Resulting suspensions |\n| `incident_count` / `sanction_count` / `suspension_count` | Integer | Dedicated stat counters for case shortcuts |\n| `subject_player_id` / `subject_club_id` / `subject_referee_id` | Many2one | Subject |\n| `summary` / `notes` | Text | Case details |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed, with under-review cases allowed back to draft for corrections before a decision is recorded.\n- **Auto-numbering** via `ir.sequence`.\n- **Counter labels** use distinct technical field names so the case relation tabs and their stat counters do not trigger duplicate-label warnings during module loading.\n\n### `federation.sanction`\n\nA penalty imposed as the outcome of a disciplinary case.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Sanction title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `sanction_type` | Selection | fine / warning / ban / point_deduction / other |\n| `player_id` / `club_id` / `referee_id` | Many2one | Who is sanctioned |\n| `amount` / `currency_id` | Monetary | For fines |\n| `effective_date` | Date | When it takes effect |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n### `federation.suspension`\n\nA time-bound match ban for a player.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Suspension title |\n| `case_id` | Many2one | Parent case |\n| `player_id` | Many2one | Suspended player |\n| `date_start` / `date_end` | Date | Ban period |\n| `state` | Selection | active / served / overturned |\n| `notes` | Text | Details |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Disciplinary Staff | Can manage incidents, cases, sanctions, and suspensions |\n\n## Data Files\n\n| File | Content |\n|------|---------|\n| `data/ir_sequence.xml` | `FED-DISC-` sequence for case reference numbers |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Incident → Case linking** — Incidents can be grouped into a case for joint handling.\n2. **Case lifecycle** — draft → under_review → decided → appealed / closed with date tracking, and under-review cases can be reopened to draft before a decision is recorded.\n3. **Multiple outcomes** — A single case can produce multiple sanctions and suspensions.\n4. **Player integration** — Inherited views add discipline tabs to player forms.\n5. **Match integration** — Inherited views add incident lists to match forms.\n6. **Finance bridge integration** — When `sports_federation_finance_bridge` is installed,\n   sanctions of type `fine` automatically create source-linked finance events and\n   keep draft amounts synchronized with sanction edits.\n", "content_length": 4687, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": +{"content": "# Sports Federation Format\n\nThe format addon manages versioned competition structures, their stages, and\nFormat Studio stage graphs.\n\n## Stage graph models\n\nFormat Studio uses `federation.structure.stage.progression` for edges between\nstages in one `federation.competition.structure`. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, and championship/relegation splits. Dynamic Swiss, ladder, and double-elimination formats are deliberately not advertised as automatic because they require round-by-round or reset-final semantics outside the immutable fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1428, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "7c527aeced8da21ff2fd2701dc53c9ce8e9d1586b33b663b7efda898a87f43dc", "size_bytes": 1428}

 {"content": "# Sports Federation Governance\n\nFormal override-request workflow with decisions and audit trails. Provides a\nstructured way for federation officials to request, review, and implement\nexceptions to standard processes.\n\n## Purpose\n\nSome situations require bending the rules — late registrations, replayed matches,\nexceptional eligibility grants. This module ensures those exceptions are\n**requested, decided, logged, and auditable** rather than happening informally.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core entities |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament references |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.override.request`\n\nA formal request to override a standard process.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Request title |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Type of override |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Linked record |\n| `requested_by_id` | Many2one | Requester (user) |\n| `requested_on` | Datetime | Request timestamp |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / submitted / approved / rejected / implemented / closed |\n| `reason` | Text | Justification |\n| `implementation_note` | Text | How it was applied |\n| `decision_ids` | One2many | Review decisions |\n| `audit_note_ids` | One2many | Audit trail entries |\n| `outcome_ids` | One2many | Post-decision outcome log |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → submitted → approved / rejected → implemented → closed, with submitted requests withdrawable back to draft before a decision is recorded.\n\n### `federation.override.decision`\n\nA review decision on an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `decision` | Selection | approve / reject / request_info |\n| `decided_by_id` | Many2one | Decision maker |\n| `decided_on` | Datetime | Decision timestamp |\n| `note` | Text | Reasoning |\n\n### `federation.audit.note`\n\nFree-form audit notes attached to an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `note` | Text | Audit remark |\n| `author_id` | Many2one | Author |\n| `created_on` | Datetime | Timestamp |\n\n### `federation.override.outcome`\n\nOutcome tracking row attached to an override request after implementation or\nfollow-up review.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | Source override request |\n| `outcome` | Selection | implemented / effective / partial / ineffective / reversed |\n| `outcome_on` | Datetime | When the outcome was recorded |\n| `recorded_by_id` | Many2one | Operator recording the outcome |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Snapshot of the originating request type |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Snapshot of the overridden record |\n| `request_state` | Selection | Request state at the time of logging |\n| `note` | Text | Outcome commentary |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Governance Officer | Can review and decide on override requests |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Formal request lifecycle** — Every exception starts as a draft request,\n   can be withdrawn back to draft while still submitted, and otherwise follows\n   a structured approval flow.\n2. **Multi-decision support** — Multiple governance officers can weigh in on a\n   single request.\n3. **Audit trail** — All decisions and notes are timestamped and attributed.\n4. **Generic target** — Requests can link to any  {"content": "# Sports Federation Reporting\n\nCross-module analytical reports backed by PostgreSQL views plus scheduled report\nsnapshots. Provides read-only report models that aggregate participation,\nofficiating, compliance, finance, and tournament-readiness data into\noperator-facing views.\n\n## Purpose\n\nGives federation administrators a **dashboard-level view** of key metrics without\nwriting SQL or building custom reports. Each report model is a database view\nthat joins and aggregates data from multiple modules into a single, filterable\nlist or pivot view, while report schedules generate recurring weekly or monthly\nCSV snapshots from inside Odoo.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Clubs, teams, seasons |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Players |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournaments |\n| `sports_federation_officiating` | Referees, assignments |\n| `sports_federation_standings` | Standings data |\n| `sports_federation_discipline` | Disciplinary data |\n| `sports_federation_compliance` | Compliance data |\n| `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Finance events |\n| `sports_federation_import_tools` | Inbound delivery failures for operator checklist reporting |\n\nAudit dashboard surfaces:\n\n- `Reporting > Portal Audit` groups privileged portal create/write/call activity\n\temitted through `federation.portal.privilege`.\n- `Reporting > Token Rotation Audit` groups manager-driven integration partner\n\ttoken rotation events emitted from the import-tools token rotation flow.\n- both dashboards read the shared `federation.audit.event` log so additional\n\taudited workflows can reuse the same reporting contract later.\n\n## Models (all SQL view-backed, `_auto = False`)\n\n### Current level |\n| `assignment_count` | Integer | Total assignments |\n| `completed_assignment_count` | Integer | Completed assignments |\n\n### `federation.report.compliance`\n\nCompliance status `missing_count` | Integer | Missing documents |\n| `pending_count` | Integer | Awaiting review |\n| `expired_count` | Integer | Expired documents |\n| `non_compliant_count` | Integer | Explicitly rejected or non-compliant checks |\n\n### `federation.report.finance`\n\nFinancial event summary by fee type and state.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `federation.report.operational`\n\nTournament-level operational KPI view.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `season_id` / `tournament_id` | Many2one | Scope of the +FILE: sports_federation_format/services/format_feasibility.py

+SHA256: 50c485edeb94be0904435fa3b207413d48364e537a83d6bb564034ad7a028526

+from math import ceil, log2
+
+from odoo import _, api, models
+
+
+class FederationFormatFeasibility(models.AbstractModel):
+    _name = "federation.format.feasibility"
+    _description = "Competition Format Feasibility"
+
+    @api.model
+    def estimate(
+        self, format_type, participant_count, *, pool_count=1, series_length=1
+    ):
+        participant_count = int(participant_count or 0)
+        pool_count = max(1, int(pool_count or 1))
+        series_length = max(1, int(series_length or 1))
+        if participant_count < 2:
+            return {
+                "feasible": False,
+                "fixture_count": 0,
+                "round_count": 0,
+                "message": _("At least two participants are required."),
+            }
+        if format_type == "single_round_robin":
+            fixtures = participant_count * (participant_count - 1) // 2
+            rounds = (
+                participant_count if participant_count % 2 else participant_count - 1
+            )
+        elif format_type == "double_round_robin":
+            fixtures = participant_count * (participant_count - 1)
+            rounds = 2 * (
+                participant_count if participant_count % 2 else participant_count - 1
+            )
+        elif format_type in ("knockout", "placement_bracket"):
+            fixtures = (participant_count - 1) * series_length
+            rounds = ceil(log2(participant_count)) * series_length
+        elif format_type == "pool_knockout":
+            if pool_count > participant_count // 2:
+                return {
+                    "feasible": False,
+                    "fixture_count": 0,
+                    "round_count": 0,
+                    "message": _("Every pool must contain at least two participants."),
+                }
+            sizes = [participant_count // pool_count] * pool_count
+            for index in range(participant_count % pool_count):
+                sizes[index] += 1
+            fixtures = (
+                sum(size * (size - 1) // 2 for size in sizes)
+                + min(participant_count, 2 * pool_count)
+                - 1
+            )
+            rounds = max(size if size % 2 else size - 1 for size in sizes) + ceil(
+                log2(min(participant_count, 2 * pool_count))
+            )
+        elif format_type == "split_pools":
+            if participant_count < 6:
+                return {
+                    "feasible": False,
+                    "fixture_count": 0,
+                    "round_count": 0,
+                    "message": _(
+                        "Split-pool competitions require at least six participants."
+                    ),
+                }
+            upper = ceil(participant_count / 2)
+            lower = participant_count - upper
+            fixtures = (
+                participant_count * (participant_count - 1) // 2
+                + upper * (upper - 1) // 2
+                + lower * (lower - 1) // 2
+            )
+            rounds = participant_count - 1 + max(upper - 1, lower - 1)
+        else:
+            return {
+                "feasible": False,
+                "fixture_count": 0,
+                "round_count": 0,
+                "message": _(
+                    "This format is configured manually and cannot be estimated automatically."
+                ),
+            }
+        return {
+            "feasible": True,
+            "fixture_count": fixtures,
+            "round_count": rounds,
+            "message": _(
+                "The format can be generated for %(teams)s participants.",
+                teams=participant_count,
+            ),
+        }
+

+class TestFormatFeasibility(TransactionCase):

+        analyzer = self.env["federation.format.feasibility"]
+        self.assertEqual(

+                analyzer.estimate("double_round_robin", 6)["round_count"],
+            ),
+            (30, 10),
+        )
+        knockout = analyzer.estimate("knockout", 8, series_length=3)
+        self.assertEqual((knockout["fixture_count"], knockout["round_count"]), (21, 9))
+

+        result = self.env["federation.format.feasibility"].estimate(

+        )
+        self.assertTrue(result["feasible"])
+        self.assertEqual((result["fixture_count"], result["round_count"]), (17, 6))
+
+    def test_impossible_formats_explain_failure(self):
+        analyzer = self.env["federation.format.feasibility"]
+        self.assertFalse(
